system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.
user_prompt:
Chapter 16: HOUSTON, WE HAVE A PROBLEM
Pages 21-22 of the book.

<<<CHAPTER TEXT

MORE ABOUT ARPEGGEIOS...{eontinued)

But I will promise you that, to whatever extent you work with this stuff, your overall
prowess on your instrument will increase in ways that you could never have guessed!

[Go For It!]

FGO...[for guitarists only] Since 4-way close is often very difficult on the guitar, all of
the above would be an excellent FIRST PASS. [As was mentioned in the text from Volume I, all
of us guitarists still should try to find as many playable voicings for 4-way close as we
can...especially using open strings.]

“HOUSTON, WE HAVE A PROBLEM...”

When you begin to work with the spread cluster material in Volume II, you may notice
a small problem. Cycles 2 and 7 have two different voice-leadings. [One for 4-way close, and
another one for the other five voicing types...] {Neither of these voice-leadings is particularly
pleasing from a sound perspective...}

We felt that this was necessary [especially for guitarists] because spread clusters present
unique voice-leading problems that don’t occur in the other 4 chord families. It involves the
interval of a diatonic 5th that occurs in the movement from one inversion to the next within
the same chord. For guitarists, this could lead to potential problems with voices crossing each
other if we had chosen to uses voice-leadings that were more pleasing from a sound perspec-
tive. Consequently, we opted for voice-leadings that at least presented the material in a useful
and somewhat “guitar-friendlier” manner, since much of this is going to be completely new to
a large percentage of the whole guitar world.

All of these spread cluster voicings are extremely interesting. [And mostly unknown,
until now...] And many of them are difficult to play on the guitar, so BE VERY CAREFUL!!!
[Other choices for voice-leading options will be presented in Volume 3.]

WHAT ABOUT VOICE-LEADING?

I'm sorry about that. I haven’t even mentioned anything about voice-leading. [I’ve
USED it, for sure...] All of the M-Lode is based on voice-leading. But to me, at this point in time
and in music history, voice-leading is not the most important thing. {At least not right
now...we'll get to voice-leading in Volume 3.}

For me, as the author, [perhaps I should describe myself as the discoverer...] the most
important thing is this :

For the first time in the history of music on our planet, all of the 3-part and 4-part
voicings that exist within the Major Scale, the Melodic Minor Scale and the Harmonic Minor
Scale have been found.


WHAT ABOUT VOICE-LEADING? (continued)

And by the time that Volume 3 is completed, published and disseminated, ALL of that
material will be not only found, but IDENTIFIED.

This is huge, in that musicians all around our planet will get the opportunity to work
with “the full deck, for the very first time...” !!

SOME NUMBERS WITH THE M-LODE...

Number of different 3-part chords found: 20

«Number of different voicings for these chords found: 240
Number of different 4-part chords found: 30+

Number of different voicings for these chords found: 800+
Total of different 3-part and 4-part voicings found: 1000+
Number of melodic movements involving a 3rd found: 276

Red, Yellow and Blue............ [Who Knew???]

I didn’t make up all of this........
I just discovered it........ {found it...}

All of this has been WAITING TO BE DISCOVERED!!
[perhaps, for thousands of years.......... ]

Frankly, I’m surprised that this Discovery hasn’t happened sooner!
[Don’t doubt the power of voice-leading or Cycles ever again...]

And it’s ALL YOURS! ! !

—HNick Goodtick 2002
